extracted.intended_audience: university health educators, faculty, graduate program directors, education researchers interested in grantsmanship
extracted.subtask_description: Analysis of a national survey of university health education faculty about their grant-writing experience, preparedness, barriers, and training offered to graduate students. Useful for understanding faculty needs and designing grant-writing training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant award prevalence and amounts
rubrics_metrics.description: This national survey of health education faculty (n = 282) found that the vast majority (88%) had been awarded a grant in the past 5 years, usually in amounts of less than $10,000. Less than one in four had received grants of $250,000 or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these prevalence and award-size data to benchmark typical grant activity among university health educators; indicates most grants obtained are small (< $10,000) and large awards (≥ $250,000) are uncommon. (Contains 5 tables.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Preparedness to write grants (post-graduation vs current)
rubrics_metrics.description: Less than one in four faculty (23%) felt prepared to write grants immediately following graduation, while four of five currently felt prepared to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights a gap between perceived readiness at graduation and later career preparedness, suggesting experiential learning or on-the-job training increases confidence; relevant when designing timing and content of grant-writing education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Barriers to grant writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Two barriers to grant writing were identified by a majority of faculty: heavy teaching loads (68%) and administrative or committee assignments (55%).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are primary impediments to faculty engaging in grant-writing; programs aiming to increase grant activity should consider workload relief, administrative support, or protected time as interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support for including grant writing in graduate training
rubrics_metrics.description: Ninety percent of the faculty thought grant writing should be part of formal graduate student training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong consensus among faculty that formal graduate curricula should include grant-writing instruction; use this as justification for curriculum development or mandatory training modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of graduate student grant-writing training
rubrics_metrics.description: Only 65% of faculty reported offering grant writing training to their graduate students, despite 90% believing it should be part of formal training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies a practice–belief gap: although most faculty endorse graduate grant-writing training, a substantial minority do not provide it. Useful metric for program evaluation and for targeting resources to increase training availability.
